why: The student says public static void main() is a fine entry point because the program uses no arguments. That is the MainWithoutStringArgs wrong rule: Java needs public static void main(String[] args) to launch, and without it java Hello reports that no main method was found.

concepts.quote: main() without String[] args is fine because the program uses no arguments.
concepts.why: This matches the MainWithoutStringArgs error edge: the header main() compiles, but the class then has no launchable entry point, so java Hello fails whether or not arguments are used.
The student only mentions arguments to defend the wrong main header and makes no claim about how args works.
The student does not explain why java Hello starts at main or what happens at launch.
